rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: If a pair of linear equations in two variables is consistent, then the lines represented by the two equations are :
rows.solution:
A consistent pair has at least one solution. The lines either meet at one point (a unique solution) or lie on top of each other (infinitely many solutions). Parallel lines never meet, so a pair of parallel lines is inconsistent.

So the lines are intersecting or coincident. This is option (D) intersecting or coincident.

rows.stem: If the area of a sector of a circle is \(\dfrac{7}{20}\) of the area of the circle, then the angle at the centre is equal to
rows.solution:
Let the angle at the centre be \(\theta\). Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2\), and this equals \(\dfrac{7}{20} \times \pi r^2\).

\(\dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \dfrac{7}{20}\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{7}{20} \times 360^\circ = 126^\circ\).

This is option (D) \(126^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. The probability of getting at most one tail is :
rows.solution:
Tossing two coins gives 4 equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.

At most one tail means zero or one tail: HH, HT and TH, which is 3 outcomes.

\(P(\text{at most one tail}) = \dfrac{3}{4}\), which is option (C) \(\dfrac{3}{4}\).

rows.stem: If the mean of five observations \(x\), \(x + 2\), \(x + 4\), \(x + 6\) and \(x + 8\) is 11, then the value of \(x\) is :
rows.solution:
Sum of the observations \(= x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) + (x + 6) + (x + 8) = 5x + 20\).

Mean \(= \dfrac{5x + 20}{5} = x + 4 = 11\), so \(x = 7\).

This is option (B) \(7\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: If the sum of first n terms of an A.P. is \(3n^2 + 4n\) and its common difference is 6, then its first term is :
rows.solution:
The first term is the sum of the first one term: \(a = S_1 = 3(1)^2 + 4(1) = 7\).

(Check: \(S_2 = 12 + 8 = 20\), so the second term is \(20 - 7 = 13\), and \(13 - 7 = 6\) is the given common difference.)

This is option (A) \(7\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: What should be subtracted from the polynomial \(x^2 - 16x + 30\), so that 15 is the zero of the resulting polynomial ?
rows.solution:
Let k be subtracted. Then 15 is a zero of \(x^2 - 16x + 30 - k\):

\(15^2 - 16 \times 15 + 30 - k = 0\), that is \(225 - 240 + 30 - k = 0\), so \(k = 15\).

This is option (C) \(15\).

\(\sec 45^\circ = \sqrt{2}\), \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\) and \(\sin 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).

\(\dfrac{\sec^2 45^\circ - \tan^2 45^\circ}{\sin^2 45^\circ} = \dfrac{(\sqrt{2})^2 - (1)^2}{\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2\).

(The numerator is 1 for any angle, since \(\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1\).)

rows.stem: Prove that \(\dfrac{\sin A + \cos A}{\sin A - \cos A} + \dfrac{\sin A - \cos A}{\sin A + \cos A} = \dfrac{2}{2\sin^2 A - 1}\)
rows.solution:
LHS \(= \dfrac{\sin A + \cos A}{\sin A - \cos A} + \dfrac{\sin A - \cos A}{\sin A + \cos A} = \dfrac{(\sin A + \cos A)^2 + (\sin A - \cos A)^2}{(\sin A - \cos A)(\sin A + \cos A)}\)

\(= \dfrac{\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A + 2\sin A\cos A + \sin^2 A + \cos^2 A - 2\sin A\cos A}{\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A}\)

\(= \dfrac{1 + 1}{\sin^2 A - (1 - \sin^2 A)}\)

\(= \dfrac{2}{2\sin^2 A - 1} =\) RHS.

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: In what ratio does the X-axis divides the line segment joining the points \((2, -3)\) and \((5, 6)\) ? Also, find the coordinates of the point of intersection.
rows.solution:
Every point on the x-axis has ordinate 0, so let the x-axis meet the segment at \((x, 0)\) and divide it in the ratio \(k : 1\).

Comparing ordinates: \(\dfrac{k(6) + 1(-3)}{k + 1} = 0\), so \(6k - 3 = 0\) and \(k = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

The ratio is \(\dfrac{1}{2} : 1\), that is \(1 : 2\).

Then \(x = \dfrac{1 \times 5 + 2 \times 2}{1 + 2} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3\), so the point of intersection is \((3, 0)\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Find the length of the median AD of \(\Delta ABC\) having vertices \(A(0, -1)\), \(B(2, 1)\) and \(C(0, 3)\).
rows.solution:
The median AD joins A to the mid-point D of BC.

\(D = \left(\dfrac{2 + 0}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 3}{2}\right) = (1, 2)\).

\(AD = \sqrt{(1 - 0)^2 + (2 - (-1))^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}\) units.

rows.stem: Through the mid-point M of the side CD of a parallelogram ABCD, the line BM is drawn intersecting AC in L and AD produced in E. Prove that EL = 2BL.
rows.solution:
Figure: parallelogram ABCD with AD produced beyond D to E; the line BE passes through the mid-point M of CD and cuts the diagonal AC at L.

Since ABCD is a parallelogram, \(AD \parallel BC\) and \(AD = BC\). E lies on AD produced, so \(AE \parallel BC\).

In triangles BMC and EMD:

\(CM = DM\) (M is the mid-point of CD),

\(\angle BMC = \angle EMD\) (vertically opposite angles),

\(\angle BCM = \angle EDM\) (alternate angles, \(BC \parallel DE\)).

So \(\Delta BMC \cong \Delta EMD\) (ASA), and \(BC = DE\) (CPCT). Then \(AE = AD + DE = BC + BC = 2BC\) ... (i)

In triangles BLC and ELA:

\(\angle LBC = \angle LEA\) (alternate angles, \(BC \parallel AE\)),

\(\angle BLC = \angle ELA\) (vertically opposite angles).

So \(\Delta BLC \sim \Delta ELA\) (AA), and \(\dfrac{BL}{EL} = \dfrac{BC}{EA}\) ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), \(\dfrac{BL}{EL} = \dfrac{BC}{2BC} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(EL = 2BL\).

rows.stem: The angle of elevation of a jet plane from a point A on the ground is \(60^\circ\). After a flight of 30 seconds, the angle of elevation changes to \(30^\circ\). If the jet plane is flying at a constant height of \(3600\sqrt{3}\) m, find the speed of the jet plane.
rows.solution:
Figure: A on the ground; P is the first position of the plane and Q its position 30 seconds later, both at height \(3600\sqrt{3}\) m; B and C are the points on the ground directly below P and Q, with A, B and C on one line. Let \(AB = x\) m and \(BC = y\) m.

In triangle APB, \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{PB}{AB}\): \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{3600\sqrt{3}}{x}\), so \(x = 3600\) m.

In triangle AQC, \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{QC}{AC}\): \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3600\sqrt{3}}{x + y}\), so \(x + y = 3600\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 10800\) m, and \(y = 10800 - 3600 = 7200\) m.

The plane flies \(PQ = BC = 7200\) m in 30 seconds.

Speed of the jet plane \(= \dfrac{7200}{30} = 240\) m/s, that is \(240 \times \dfrac{18}{5} = 864\) km/h.
